newsitem.title: BRAZIL: More debt may be allowed in Banerj sale.
newsitem.headline: More debt may be allowed in Banerj sale.

text.p: Brazil's Rio de Janeiro state said it may expand the amount of privatization bonds that investors are allowed to use to buy control of state bank Banerj.
The move would make it cheaper for investors to buy Banerj while maintaining the state's promise not to reduce the 480 million-real base price, according to analysts.

Under current rules, bidders may pay up to 30 million reais of the purchase price for Banerj and its insurance unit Banerj Seguros using Privatization Certificates, representing state securitized debt.

A spokesman for Rio's planning office said the state will consider a proposal to allow investors to use more debt paper in Banerj's auction as it revises all rules for the bank's selloff before publication of new bid specifications this month.
The use of more debt to buy Banerj would make it cheaper because Brazilian privatization bonds are traded at a discount on the secondary market, analysts said.
After two failed attempts in December, Rio now hopes to privatize Banerj in February. The bank would be the first Brazilian state bank to be sold to the private sector.
